items.name: Iron ore
items.description: Highland ore. Smelts into the plate everything else is built from.

items.name: Component
items.description: A plate-mounted gear mechanism for the landing hub and mechanical supply requests.

items.name: Signal crystal
items.description: A finite highland seam no hand can cut. Place an extractor on the field; the deep arm is what a thin seam is for.

items.name: Copper ore
items.description: Hill ore. Becomes the plate and wire every circuit needs.

items.name: Coal
items.description: Dense highland fuel, and the carbon steel is made with.

items.name: Stone
items.description: Cut from cliff faces. The cheapest structural material there is.

items.name: Sand
items.description: Shore grit. Melts into glass and binds into concrete.

items.name: Clay
items.description: Damp shore and lowland earth. Fires into brick.

items.name: Wood
items.description: Cut from lowland flora, which grows back. Burns, and cuts into timber.

items.name: Water
items.description: Pumped from a basin as loose fluid. Route it through pipes or seal ten units in a water barrel; fresh belts reject it.

items.name: Iron plate
items.description: Smelted iron. The structural backbone of every later tier.

items.name: Copper plate
items.description: Smelted copper, drawn into wire.

items.name: Glass
items.description: Melted sand. The substrate a circuit is printed on.

items.name: Brick
items.description: Fired clay. Cheap, plentiful, and it holds heat.

items.name: Charcoal
items.description: Wood pyrolysed into fuel, so smelting never waits on a coal field.

items.name: Timber
items.description: Wood cut to length. Frames are built from it.

items.name: Gravel
items.description: Crushed stone. Aggregate for concrete.

items.name: Copper wire
items.description: Drawn copper. Three of them and a pane of glass make a circuit.

items.name: Gear
items.description: Cut iron teeth. The first part that is a mechanism rather than a material.

items.name: Frame
items.description: Timber braced with iron. Everything large is hung on one.

items.name: Concrete
items.description: Cement bound with gravel, sand and water. The binder is what makes a slab hold, and the basin is still required.

items.name: Circuit
items.description: Glass printed with copper. Where the material base starts to think.

items.name: Steel
items.description: Iron smelted again with coal. The strongest thing this world makes.

items.name: Transport kit
items.description: A bundle of belting, rollers and fittings. One kit lays one belt; a corner heading takes two. Made a batch at a time from a plate and a length of timber.

items.name: Iron wire
items.description: Drawn iron. A poorer conductor than copper, which is why first-generation power equipment is bulky — but it comes from the ore under the landing site instead of an expedition to the copper band.

items.name: Limestone
items.description: Hill quarry stone. Burned with clay into cement; not the same rock as the cliff scree you already cut.

items.name: Cement
items.description: Kiln-fired binder. Turns gravel, sand and water into concrete, and holds a brick wall together.

items.name: Crude oil
items.description: Finite lowland oil deposit. A powered oil well extracts it as loose fluid; route it through pipes or seal ten units in an oil barrel.

items.name: Bitumen
items.description: Road binder from the refinery. Every two bitumen also produce two refined fuel; route each product through its own footprint port.

items.name: Refined fuel
items.description: Useful refinery co-product. Feed a burner generator, boiler or heated recipe. Oil energy is released here; the refinery needs electricity, not a coal ingredient.

items.name: Asphalt
items.description: Bitumen-bound aggregate. Two units pave one hex over a gravel base in Ground works, for 50% faster walking. Stored ready to lay; not an upper floor.

items.name: Empty barrel
items.description: A reusable sealed drum. A barrel station fills it with ten units of water or crude oil and returns it when emptied.

items.name: Water barrel
items.description: Ten units of water sealed for belt transport. Empty it at a barrel station to recover both the water and reusable drum.

items.name: Oil barrel
items.description: Ten units of crude oil sealed for belt transport. Empty it at a barrel station beside the consuming pipe network.

items.name: Pipe section
items.description: Iron tube and couplings for one fluid-pipe segment. A corner heading covers twice the ground and takes two sections.

recipes.name: Compose component
recipes.description: Mount one gear on an iron plate to make a mechanical component.

recipes.name: Smelt iron plate
recipes.description: Melt two iron ore down into one plate.

recipes.name: Smelt copper plate
recipes.description: Melt two copper ore down into one plate.

recipes.name: Melt glass
recipes.description: Melt two sand into one pane of glass.

recipes.name: Smelt steel
recipes.description: Smelt two iron plate with two coal as carbon. The heat is fuel on top of that.

recipes.name: Fire brick
recipes.description: Fire two clay into three brick.

recipes.name: Char wood
recipes.description: Pyrolyse six wood into charcoal. The kiln burns most of the charge to cook the rest, so charcoal is denser than the wood it came from — never richer.

recipes.name: Cut timber
recipes.description: Cut one wood into two lengths of timber.

recipes.name: Crush gravel
recipes.description: Crush one stone into two gravel.

recipes.name: Draw copper wire
recipes.description: Draw one copper plate into two lengths of wire.

recipes.name: Cut gear
recipes.description: Cut two iron plate into one toothed gear.

recipes.name: Build frame
recipes.description: Brace two timber with an iron plate.

recipes.name: Mix concrete
recipes.description: Bind two gravel, one sand and one water with one cement into two concrete.

recipes.name: Print circuit
recipes.description: Print three copper wire onto a pane of glass.

recipes.name: Assemble transport kits
recipes.description: Cut one iron plate and one timber into four belt kits. The batch is what makes a line affordable.

recipes.name: Draw iron wire
recipes.description: Draw one iron plate into two lengths of wire. The conductor a first generator and its poles are wound with, before copper is worth the walk.

recipes.name: Fire cement
recipes.description: Burn two limestone with one clay into two cement. The kiln supplies the heat; nothing here is mixed wet.

recipes.name: Refine crude oil
recipes.description: Separate four crude oil into two bitumen and two refined fuel. Both products share the output buffer but may leave through separate chosen footprint ports. Cost allocation: bitumen 50%, fuel 50% of the whole batch.

recipes.name: Mix asphalt
recipes.description: Bind three gravel with one bitumen into four asphalt. Lay it over a gravel base in Ground works; no curing timer.

recipes.name: Form empty barrel
recipes.description: Roll and seal two iron plates into one reusable barrel.

recipes.name: Form pipe sections
recipes.description: Roll one iron plate into two coupled pipe sections.

recipes.name: Fill water barrel
recipes.description: Seal ten units of piped water in one empty barrel for belt transport.

recipes.name: Empty water barrel
recipes.description: Return one reusable barrel and ten units of loose water for a pipe network.

recipes.name: Fill oil barrel
recipes.description: Seal ten units of piped crude oil in one empty barrel for belt transport.

recipes.name: Empty oil barrel
recipes.description: Return one reusable barrel and ten units of loose crude oil for a pipe network.

buildings.name: Extractor
buildings.description: Harvests every field cell within one hex and emits one item at a time. Slower than your own hands on the same material — but it never stops, and you can walk away. Built from plate, a gear and timber, all of which a primitive furnace and workshop already make.

buildings.name: Belt
buildings.description: Moves one cargo stack along its heading. Built from one transport kit; Corner Transport adds the six vertex headings between them, which span two rows for twice the price.

buildings.name: Composer
buildings.description: Assembles parts from finished materials. Needs no fuel. It is the workshop's bench built properly, and it is billed that way: plate, a gear and a frame, with no signal crystal to fetch first.

buildings.name: Container
buildings.description: Buffers exact item quantities and releases the lowest item ID first. A timber crate; the deep container is the metal one.

buildings.name: Demo receiver
buildings.description: Scenario-owned receiver retained for the factory demo.

buildings.name: Landing hub
buildings.description: Accepts deliveries, awards insight, and tracks the native objective.

buildings.name: Smelter
buildings.description: Melts ore and sand. Burns any fuel item fed to it.

buildings.name: Kiln
buildings.description: Fires clay and chars wood. Burns any fuel item fed to it.

buildings.name: Cutter
buildings.description: Cuts wood to length. Needs no fuel.

buildings.name: Crusher
buildings.description: Crushes stone into aggregate. Needs no fuel.

buildings.name: Pump
buildings.description: Draws from the named water cell beside it. Finite ponds drain; a river replenishes up to its rated discharge.

buildings.name: Pole
buildings.description: Connects machines and generators into one power network. A timber mast strung with iron wire; the relay pole is where copper starts to pay.

buildings.name: Burner generator
buildings.description: Burns any fuel item into electricity. Holds 12 fuel — feed it by belt or by hand. Wound with iron wire, which is why it is bulky and why first power needs no copper.

buildings.name: Wind turbine
buildings.description: Fuel-free power on hills and highland — the same ground the ore sits on.

buildings.name: Hydro generator
buildings.description: High output at a basin edge. Scarce, because the shore is scarce. A rotor and its gearing, braced on a frame — the river turns it, so nothing here is fired and nothing is laid in brick.

buildings.name: Boiler
buildings.description: Burns fuel and piped water into steam for an adjacent turbine. Aim a pipe at its footprint and keep the water input buffered.

buildings.name: Steam turbine
buildings.description: Turns an adjacent boiler into the mid-game workhorse. Place it beside the boiler.

buildings.name: Deep extractor
buildings.description: Reaches two hexes instead of one and works twice as fast, which is the moment a machine finally matches your own hands. The arm is visible on the map: one deep extractor works a field a ring of shallow ones could not.

buildings.name: Deep container
buildings.description: Twice the buffer in the same hex, for a line that outruns what one container can hold. Plated and braced over a stone footing, built from the same timber the first container is.

buildings.name: Relay pole
buildings.description: Lights a wider disc and spans further to the next pole. Every machine already standing in the new ring joins the network the moment the pole grows.

buildings.name: Trunk pole
buildings.description: Carries a grid across open country: six hexes of coverage and twelve to the next trunk. What a distant site costs is a line of these rather than a second power plant.

buildings.name: Bridge
buildings.description: Decks one shallow-water hex so transport can cross it. Deep water remains a barrier.

buildings.name: Splitter
buildings.description: A belt that also feeds the two headings either side of the one it faces, handing each stack to the next output that will take it. A blocked branch is skipped rather than waited on, so one full line never stalls the others.

buildings.name: Merger
buildings.description: A belt that takes from the lines feeding it in turn rather than in the order they were built, so two lanes joining here share the throughput instead of one starving the other.

buildings.name: Underpass
buildings.description: Drag from entrance to exit to place one atomic portal pair. Cargo dives beneath up to four occupied hexes while the crossing lane stays independent; a click still places one ordinary endpoint.

buildings.name: Primitive Furnace
buildings.description: Smelt iron and copper plates with ordinary fuel and no electricity. Twice the industrial craft time. Built from local stone and clay; recoverable by dismantling.

buildings.name: Manual Workshop
buildings.description: Stand beside this bench, load ingredients, and choose Work one batch. Make timber, transport kits, components, gears, frames, and drawn iron wire at four times industrial craft time — every part the first extractor, composer, generator and pole are billed in. Walking or gathering pauses work; dismantling recovers reserved ingredients.

buildings.name: Oil well
buildings.description: A powered well for finite lowland oil deposits. Produces loose crude oil: supply electricity and run a pipe from its outlet toward a tank or refinery. Built from existing metalwork; no oil is needed to obtain the first oil.

buildings.name: Refinery
buildings.description: Separates crude into bitumen and refined fuel in equal quantities. Select each product in the inspector and assign an outside port on either footprint tile. If either stream backs up, the refinery waits without losing anything.

buildings.name: Asphalt mixer
buildings.description: Mixes gravel and bitumen into ready-to-lay asphalt. Two asphalt pave a hex over a gravel base in Ground works. A fast-road specialty; brick and concrete construction remain oil-free.

buildings.name: Pipe
buildings.description: Carries one unit of loose water or crude oil per segment and tick. Drag from a source toward a consumer; solids and filled barrels stay on belts.

buildings.name: Pipe underpass
buildings.description: Drag from entrance to exit to place an atomic pair. Loose fluid dives beneath up to four occupied hexes; the crossing lane stays independent.

buildings.name: Water tank
buildings.description: Buffers up to 120 units of loose water and nothing else. Aim its outlet toward a pipe; use barrels when the route must ride a belt.

buildings.name: Oil tank
buildings.description: Buffers up to 120 units of loose crude oil and nothing else. It accepts pipes, not filled barrels or unrelated stock.

buildings.name: Barrel station
buildings.description: Fills or empties reusable water and oil barrels. Route loose contents by pipe and sealed barrels by belt; assign separate output ports when emptying.

requests.name: Ore assay
requests.brief: The survey wants a proper sample of the highland seam before the hub commits a foundry to it.

requests.name: Cliff stone
requests.brief: Cut stone for the landing pad's apron. The cliff faces are the nearest source, and the nearest is what the hub is paying for.

requests.name: Cordwood
requests.brief: Lowland wood, unworked. The hub burns it while there is nothing better to burn, and the flora grows back.

requests.name: Clay survey
requests.brief: Wet shore earth, for a kiln nobody has built yet. Bring enough to prove the bed is worth siting on.

requests.name: Shore sand
requests.brief: Shore grit, for the glass that comes before circuits and the concrete that comes after them.

requests.name: Coal seam
requests.brief: Highland coal. Every furnace and every burner in this world eventually asks for it, so the hub wants its own pile.

requests.name: Copper assay
requests.brief: The hills carry copper as well as iron, and nothing here conducts a signal without it.

requests.name: Crystal array
requests.brief: Signal crystal is finite and no recipe makes more. The hub wants a reserve while the fields still hold some.

requests.name: Plate stock
requests.brief: Smelted iron, not ore. The hub is paying for the smelting, and it pays better than the digging did.

requests.name: Copper stock
requests.brief: Copper run through the same furnace. Plate travels better than ore and is worth more when it lands.

requests.name: Kiln brick
requests.brief: Fired clay for a furnace lining. A kiln turns two clay into three bricks, so this bill is cheaper than its number looks.

requests.name: Glazing panes
requests.brief: Melted sand. Nobody can be asked for a circuit until somebody can make a pane.

requests.name: Charcoal run
requests.brief: Wood pyrolysed into fuel, so a furnace sited far from any coal can still run. Six logs a lump, and the hub pays for every one of them.

requests.name: Sawn timber
requests.brief: Wood cut to length. One log makes two, which is the first recipe in this world that hands back more than it took.

requests.name: Ballast
requests.brief: Crushed stone for the pad's bed. A crusher doubles it, so one cliff face goes twice as far.

requests.name: Component batch
requests.brief: Plate-mounted gear mechanisms. The larger payment covers their smelting and mechanical work.

requests.name: Drawn wire
requests.brief: Copper drawn thin. Three of them and one pane make a circuit, and the hub is counting ahead.

requests.name: Cut gears
requests.brief: Iron plate cut into teeth. The first thing here that is a mechanism rather than a material.

requests.name: Braced frames
requests.brief: Timber braced with iron: two chains from two landscapes meeting in one machine, which is what this bill is really testing.

requests.name: Concrete pour
requests.brief: Cement-bound concrete. The hub is paying for the quarry, the kiln and the basin together.

requests.name: Circuit batch
requests.brief: Glass printed with copper. Nothing in this one is close to the ground, which is exactly why it pays.

requests.name: Steel billets
requests.brief: Iron smelted a second time with coal. The strongest thing this world makes, at the end of its longest chain.

requests.name: Hill limestone
requests.brief: Quarried hill stone, not cliff scree. The hub wants a binder feedstock before anyone pours a slab.

requests.name: Bagged cement
requests.brief: Kiln-fired binder. Two limestone and one clay make two bags, and the hub is buying the firing.

requests.name: Road binder
requests.brief: Deliver eight bitumen from a working refinery. The same batches make eight fuel; keep that stream moving too.

requests.name: Useful side stream
requests.brief: Refining has two useful outputs. Deliver eight refined fuel once; burn later batches in compatible power equipment.

requests.name: Petroleum roads
requests.brief: Supply sixteen asphalt for a logistics apron. Make it from gravel and refinery bitumen; the petroleum branch is optional.

boundaries.name: Timber fence
boundaries.description: Two rails mark a boundary and block walking and transport across its edge. Leaves both hexes free. Make timber at the manual workshop.

boundaries.name: Timber gate
boundaries.description: A manual, unpowered crossing. Built open; close it when the edge is clear. Timber and iron wire are both made at the manual workshop.

boundaries.name: Timber wall
boundaries.description: A solid boarded wall. It still leaves both hexes free, but you cannot see through it. Four lengths of timber from the manual workshop.

boundaries.name: Wire fence
boundaries.description: Timber posts and iron wire. See through the enclosure; still blocks walking and transport. Wire is drawn at the manual workshop.

boundaries.name: Wire gate
boundaries.description: A see-through manual crossing. Built open. Timber and iron wire are both made at the manual workshop.

boundaries.name: Brick wall
boundaries.description: Fired brick set in cement. The first masonry enclosure: opaque, oil-free, and it leaves both hexes free.

boundaries.name: Brick gate
boundaries.description: A masonry doorway with a manual, unpowered leaf. Built open. Research Fired Masonry; brick and cement come from the kiln.

boundaries.name: Concrete wall
boundaries.description: A poured industrial enclosure. Two concrete, which now means cement, aggregate, sand and water.

surfaces.name: Compacted earth
surfaces.description: Tamped dirt, no materials needed. A tenth faster than raw ground and the cheapest way to learn where your paths actually run.

surfaces.name: Gravel yard
surfaces.description: Crushed stone spread and rolled flat. A fifth faster than raw ground. Crush stone into gravel at the manual workshop.

surfaces.name: Timber decking
surfaces.description: Planks laid over the ground. A quarter faster than raw ground, and made from wood you already cut.

surfaces.name: Brick pavers
surfaces.description: Fired brick set in a bed of sand. A quarter faster than raw ground, and it does not rot underfoot.

surfaces.name: Concrete slab
surfaces.description: Poured and cured. A durable oil-free yard with 30% faster walking than raw ground.

surfaces.name: Asphalt road
surfaces.description: A fast logistics road, not a structural floor. Lay over a gravel yard: the base stays paid into the road and comes back when stripped. Two asphalt per hex; 50% faster than raw ground.
